### 1. Hubstaff Chromebook Compatibility & Supported Options

* **Compatibility Conclusion**: You **cannot** perform a normal desktop client installation on a Chromebook. Hubstaff’s full desktop app is restricted to Windows, macOS, and Linux.
* **Supported ChromeOS Options**:
  1. **Hubstaff Chrome Extension**: Hubstaff’s primary supported option for ChromeOS, installed directly via the Chrome Web Store.
  2. **Web Timer**: A zero-install browser dashboard alternative that tracks basic time.
* **Feature Limitations on Chromebook**:
  * The Chrome Extension cannot perform full desktop-level monitoring. Screenshots are no longer supported on the extension (deprecated since version 0.10.1).
  * Activity tracking has a 15-second granularity (any action in a 15-second window registers as 100% active).
  * Keystrokes and mouse movements cannot be split into separate percentages (both show identical values due to OS/browser API limitations).

---

### 2. Official Brave Chromebook Install Link & Methods

Because ChromeOS lacks a native standalone `.apk`-less desktop package on Brave’s general download page, Brave supports Chromebooks through two official routes:

1. **Full Desktop Brave via Linux (Recommended for extensions & desktop UI)**:
   * **Official Setup Link**: [https://brave.com/linux/](https://brave.com/linux/)
   * **Procedure**: Turn on the Linux development environment (Crostini) in Chromebook Settings, open the Terminal, and run the Debian/Ubuntu setup commands:
     ```bash
     sudo apt install curl
     sudo curl -fsSLo /usr/share/keyrings/brave-browser-archive-keyring.gpg https://brave-browser-apt-release.s3.brave.com/brave-browser-archive-keyring.gpg
     sudo curl -fsSLo /etc/apt/sources.list.d/brave-browser-release.sources https://brave-browser-apt-release.s3.brave.com/brave-browser.sources
     sudo apt update
     sudo apt install brave-browser
     ```
     *(Or via the one-line installer: `curl -fsS https://dl.brave.com/install.sh | sh`)*
   * **Official Brave Community Guide**: [Installing Brave Browser on Chrome OS with Linux](https://community.brave.app/t/installing-brave-browser-on-chrome-os-with-linux/483352)
2. **Android App via Google Play Store**:
   * Official Play Store listing page: [https://brave.com/android/](https://brave.com/android/)

### 3. Chrome DevTools AI Assistance: Getting Started & Data Usage

#### Getting Started
* **Prerequisites**:
  * User must be at least 18 years old and located in a supported region (such as the US).
  * Running the latest Chrome release and signed into Chrome with a Google Account.
  * DevTools language set to **English (US)** under `Settings > Preferences > Appearance > Language`.
  * AI innovations toggled on under DevTools `Settings > AI Innovations`.
* **How to Use**: Open the **AI assistance** panel from the DevTools menu. It integrates Gemini directly into DevTools for:
  * **Elements / CSS**: Diagnosing layout issues, explaining styles, and suggesting CSS fixes.
  * **Network Panel**: Investigating request failures, latency, and headers.
  * **Sources Panel**: Explaining loaded scripts and code flow.
  * **Performance Panel**: Analyzing traces, LCP bottlenecks, and function call frames.

#### What Data It Uses & Privacy Controls
* **General Data**: Your prompt text, uploaded screenshots, Google Account authentication data, and thumbs up/down feedback. Data may be retained for up to 18 months and, for standard consumer accounts, reviewed by human evaluators to train AI models.
* **Context-Specific Technical Data**:
  * *Console*: Error messages, log levels, stack traces, and relevant code fragments.
  * *Network*: Target URLs, response status codes, timing data, and safe headers (sensitive headers such as `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `Authorization`, and custom `X-*` headers as well as response bodies are excluded).
  * *Elements & Sources*: Inspected DOM node structures, CSS rules, file names, URLs, and relevant source code fragments.
* **Enterprise & Privacy Policy**:
  * Governed by the `DevToolsGenAiSettings` policy.
  * Setting value `0`: Enabled with model improvement (default for consumers).
  * Setting value `1`: Enabled without model training (default for Chrome Enterprise and Workspace Education; user data is not used for model training).
  * Setting value `2`: Completely disables AI assistance features across DevTools.

---

### 4. Chrome Opening in Guest Mode: Step-by-Step Fixes

If Chrome repeatedly defaults to Guest mode instead of your normal profile, follow these recovery steps:

1. **Fix Pinned Shortcuts & App Launchers**:
   * If Chrome was pinned to the taskbar, dock, or shelf while a Guest window was open, the shortcut may be hardcoded to Guest mode.
   * **Fix**: Right-click and unpin Chrome. Open Chrome cleanly from the application menu or launcher, click your user avatar to ensure you are in your normal profile, then re-pin that window.
2. **Remove the `--guest` Command-Line Switch**:
   * Inspect the launcher/shortcut target properties:
     * *Windows*: Right-click shortcut > **Properties** > inspect the **Target** field.
     * *macOS / Linux*: Check desktop files or terminal aliases.
   * **Fix**: Remove `--guest` if appended. To lock the shortcut to your profile, append `--profile-directory="Default"` (or your profile folder name).
3. **Bypass the Profile Picker on Startup**:
   * If Chrome opens to the "Who's using Chrome?" window, click directly on your profile picture/initial instead of "Browse as Guest".
   * In the bottom-right corner of the Profile Picker, **uncheck "Show on startup"** so Chrome automatically opens your default profile on subsequent launches.
4. **Disable Guest Browsing in ChromeOS Settings (Chromebook Specific)**:
   * Open Chromebook **Settings** > **Security and privacy** > **Manage other people**.
   * Toggle off **"Enable Guest browsing"**.
   * Turn on **"Restrict sign-in to the following users"** and ensure your primary Google account is added as the owner.
5. **Check Managed Device Policies**:
   * Navigate to `chrome://policy` in the address bar.
   * Check if `BrowserGuestModeEnforced` or `DeviceGuestModeEnabled` is set to `true`. If set by an administrator or legacy registry key, clear or reset that policy.
6. **Reset Corrupted Profile / Sync State**:
   * If your local profile data is corrupted, Chrome may fail to load it and drop back to Guest mode.
   * Go to `chrome://settings/reset` and select **"Restore settings to their original defaults"**, or clear corrupted sync data at [chrome.google.com/sync](https://chrome.google.com/sync) before signing back in.
